sources.title: Compound prism design principles, I
sources.locator: Section 3 Eq. (1); Section 9 Double Amici Prisms, Fig. 10 and Eq. (14); Fig. 13
sources.verifiedContent: Three-element symmetric compound prisms use the same outer glasses. Direct vision requires the central wavelength exit angle to equal the entrance angle; four-interface nonlinear Snell refraction, glass dispersion and aperture geometry matter. Dispersion can be nonlinear.
sources.evidenceLayer: primary peer-reviewed general optics, not this instrument's internal construction

sources.title: MKS Newport: The Grating Equation
sources.verifiedContent: Transmission orders lie opposite the incident side of the grating. Orders are discrete integers; zero order is not dispersed. With normal incidence, sin(theta_m)=m*lambda*line_density. The rays disperse in a plane perpendicular to the grooves, and angular dispersion is not exactly linear in wavelength.
